Unlike Caco-2 cell assays, PAMPA has no active transporters, no efflux pumps, and no paracellular pathway — it isolates pure passive diffusion. The NCATS variant uses a standardized protocol across a large compound library.

The rate of passive diffusion is governed by the drug's ability to partition from aqueous solution into the lipid bilayer, diffuse across it, and re-partition into the aqueous phase on the other side. Features associated with poor PAMPA permeability: high TPSA (>120 Å²) is the dominant negative predictor. Multiple hydrogen bond donors (HBD ≥ 4) strongly reduce permeability. Charged species at the assay pH (typically pH 7.4) — carboxylates, phosphates, quaternary amines — have very poor passive diffusion because the charge cannot be buried in the lipid interior.
